section.sectionSummaryBrief: The maamar explains that the soul does not need rectification because it stands in its image before the Holy King and was in ultimate attachment to its source, representing two levels of nullification.
section.t: And it is explained in the maamar,
that this—that the soul does not require rectification—
is,
because every single soul stands in its image before the Holy King,
and it adds,
that the soul, before it descended below, was in ultimate attachment to its source in the living God,
in true attachment and constant attachment without any separation whatsoever.
For these two matters
(stands in its image before the Holy King and that it was in ultimate attachment)
are two levels in the nullification of the soul.
"Stands etc. before the Holy King" is like one standing before the king.
For although when one stands before the king he is nullified utterly,
for one who gestures before the king becomes the opposite of his vitality to him,
nevertheless,
from his own perspective he is an entity, and his nullification is only because he stands before the king.
And this—that the soul is in ultimate attachment etc.—is
that it is not an entity unto itself.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The maamar adds that before its descent the soul was in one will with Hashem alone, and the question is raised what this adds beyond ultimate attachment.
section.t: And the maamar adds, after it says that the soul before its descent was in ultimate attachment etc.,
that it was in one will with Hashem alone, and there is no alien will with Him.
And it needs to be understood,
that after it says that it is in ultimate attachment,
what does it add and innovate by saying that it has no alien will.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This is explained through the Gemara about Yaakov and his sons, raising questions about the equality and nature of their nullification.
section.t: And this is to be explained based on what is stated in the Gemara:
Yaakov sought to reveal to his sons the end of days, and the Shechinah departed from him.
He said,
"Perhaps, Heaven forbid, there is a blemish in my bed,"
His sons said to him, etc., "Just as there is only One in your heart, so too there is only One in our hearts."
And it needs to be understood,
Behold, the nullification of the tribes
("there is only One in our hearts")
is lower in level than the nullification of Yaakov
[and as is understood from this very thing that Yaakov
(the attribute of truth)
was in doubt, lest there be a blemish in his bed],
yet the language "just as... so too" indicates that the two matters are equal.
Also, it needs to be understood,
what they said, "there is only One in your heart,"
behold, the nullification of the Patriarchs—they are the Chariot—
[and all the more so that of Yaakov,
the chosen of the Patriarchs]
was in all the limbs of the body,
so why did they say "there is only One in your heart"?
And even more so it is not understood,
for the explanation of "b'libcha"
(your heart)
(with the letter beis)
is "what is within your heart"
[similar to the explanation of "b'kol"],
for from this it implies that even in the heart of Yaakov,
the matter of "only One" is only in the innerness of the heart.
